text:
alex: ran a ~2min nsys trace on the long-seq perf job; huge HBM bandwidth spike at t=18s when a 2k-seq batch hit. kernel timeline shows attention_fuse_v2 stepping in, then fallback to generic_gemm after L2 thrash. attaching quick summary below.

mai: ugh, that matches the regression we started seeing after kernel-selector tweak last week. any chance the selector is picking fp16-cudnn path for those seqs?

alex: not cudnn — the trace shows our custom fused attention was chosen first, then a bunch of memcpy/kernel retries. perfbot attached the nsys slice.

perfbot: nsys summary: total HBM BW peak 710 GB/s; sustained 420 GB/s for 230ms window. Top kernels by BW:
- attention_fuse_v2 (peak 310 GB/s)
- kv_read_prefetch (peak 180 GB/s)
- generic_gemm (peak 120 GB/s)
Note: KV prefetch launches concurrent loads across pages, causing HBM read storms with long sequences.

sam: can you paste the nsys cli used? want to repro locally.

alex: sure:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --capture-range=kernel --sample=none -o kv-longseq e2e_longseq_runner --env TRACE=1
```
plus perfetto recording of host timeline for the same run. link: https://perfetto.local/trace/2418/kv-longseq (short link)

tess: quick idea — our KV cache coalescing window is 16 pages; with 2k sequences the readset crosses many page boundaries causing interleaved DMA and kernel contention. increasing coalesce window to 64 reduced syscall churn last time. can we try that?

alex: I tried bumping coalesce_window to 64 and re-ran a short repro. bandwidth peak dropped ~18% but latency tail worsened for p99. p50 improved. so it's a tradeoff: bigger coalesce reduces BW burst but increases per-request latency due to larger prefetch set.

mai: what about microbatching heuristics? if we split those long seqs into smaller microbatches we can avoid the simultaneous large KV read spikes. Is the scheduler respecting sequence-length-aware packing?

alex: scheduler currently uses token-count packing but packs up to 8 samples per microbatch. For these cases, packing aggregates many long sequences into the same microbatch and triggers a worst-case readset. I pushed a flag to prefer seq-length bucketing: pack similar-lengths together. experiment results: p99 latency down 12%, HBM bursts smoother.

perfbot: run diffs (short):
- kernel-selector: minor tweak to prefer fused_attention for avg_seq<512, fallback unchanged
- scheduler: enable seq-bucketing opt-in flag
- kvcache: coalesce_window=64 on branch
Observed: fixture with mixed seqs (p95=820, p99=1800) -> BW peak -22%, p99 latency -11% vs main.

jen: nice. any hot kernels remaining in the flame?

alex: generic_gemm still shows higher occupancy in the middle of the timeline — seems like when fused attention falls back the GEMM path does lots of small launches instead of a single large call; looking into kernel-launch overhead + small-GEMM tiling. also NVTX markers reveal heavy sampler contention in the region where KV prefetch completes.

sam: next steps I propose:
1) run an nsys with kernel-stack capturing for the fallback region to see why fused path fails (OOM? bank conflicts?)
2) add a scheduler cap for mixing >1 seq>1024 in same microbatch as a short-term mitigation
3) prototype a streaming-kv-read mode that pages KV into L2-friendly chunks rather than all-at-once prefetch

mai: agree. Alex, can you queue 2) as a config rollout so we can A/B test impact on production traces? small percentage to start.

alex: queued config flag as `packer.max_highseq_per_microbatch=1` and rolled to 5% staging. I'll attach nsys traces from the A variants once available.

tess: also throw in a small kernel selector metric that records "fallback_reason" (e.g., tile_mismatch, l2_eviction, workspace_oom) to help correlate.

alex: good call — added a perf event tag to the kernel selector. will re-run nightly and share the traces.

perfbot: note: schedule created for extended profiling run tonight (8pm PT) with perfetto + nsys; notify #eng-runtime after 9pm if you want the live viewer. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

jen: thanks team — this looks actionable. Alex, please drop the perf links in this thread when ready and tag me for follow-up on kernel tiling changes.

alex: will do. thanks all.
